newsitem.title: USA: Chino mine talks still unresolved amid picketing.
newsitem.headline: Chino mine talks still unresolved amid picketing.

text.p: The labor talks stalemate at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine in New Mexico continues amid weekly picketing of the plant manager's office, union officials said.
Unionised workers at the Chino 169,000 tons per year copper mine and SX/EW plant have been without a labor contract since June 30 last year.

Robert Guadiana, lead negotiator at the United Steelworkers of America, said Phelps had refused to meet the union leaders in Silver City where the operations are based, and now both sides were trying to fix a meeting elsewhere.
The union has requested information about rates of pay and benefits at non-unionised facilities to verify Phelps view that Chino employees were among the best paid in the industry.
Phelps was unable to comment immediately.
The company offered a four-year pay freeze contract to the workers last August. It was the final offer, Phelps said at the time.
Guadiana said the union has filed charges with the National Labor Relations Board against Phelps because the "company was adamant they don't have to provide that information."
Guadiana said there were other activities proposed but declined to specify them. Chino operations were working normally at present, he added.
The unions have also placed advertisements in local newspapers about their campaign.
"It's starting to get ugly out there," Guadiana said. "But I'd rather settle the thing and move on."
